the noncommutativity of space–time is a source of new physical phenomena and that these phenomena can be understood in the framework of a noncommutative field theory that is equivalent to the ordinary commutative field theory.

the noncommutativity of spacetime leads to the appearance of a new type of gauge symmetry, the noncommutatively induced gauge symmetry, which can be interpreted as a noncommutatively deformed version of the conformal symmetry, and that the noncommuttative deformation of spacetime leads in general to the breaking of the conformal invariance of the classical action.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Seiberg-Wittens map is not a one-to-one correspondence between the noncommutativedeformed theory and its commutative limit.
